cells.quote: The majority of coaches support several teachers at a time; nearly half of school-based coaches serve more than 16 teachers at one time, while 65 percent of district-based coaches serve more than 16 teachers concurrently (see Figure 9).
cells.note: Descriptive comparison from a national online survey; groups were not randomly assigned.

D.treatment: more time spent with the coach
D.comparison: less time spent with the coach

cells.quote: On average, teachers who spend more time with their coach rate their coaching as very or highly valuable (see Figure 17).
cells.note: The survey reports an association between contact time and perceived coaching value, not a causal effect.

O.outcome_detail: reported use of technology to facilitate coaching and support educator technology learning

cells.quote: Despite the previous research on the importance of coaching for impactful technology use, nearly 40 percent fewer teachers than coaches report in the national coaching survey that technology is used to facilitate the coach’s work, support the educator’s learning, and support educators in using technology with students for learning (see Figures 12 and 13).
cells.note: This is a difference between coach and teacher self-reports, not a randomized comparison.

cells.quote: Forty-three percent of district-based administrators reported that coaches are funded multi-year, compared to 37 percent of school-based administrators (see Figure 22).
cells.note: Descriptive survey comparison of reported funding timelines; no causal effect is established.
